questions.question: Sound cannot travel through ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Sound cannot travel through a **vacuum**__. A vacuum has no mass and the pressure is o N/m².
 
• The speed of sound in air is 343 m/s.
 
• Since there is no matter in vacuum for the vibrations to work, the sound cannot travel through it.
 
• Sound can be produced only when there are vibrations present in a material body.
 
• Unlike sound, light waves are EM waves(electromagnetic waves) and can travel through any medium.
 
• The speed of light is 3 *10⁸ m/s.

questions.question: Which of the following creatures use ultrasonic sound to catch their prey?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Bats**__ use ultrasonic sound to catch their prey at night.
 
• They emit ultrasonic waves with higher frequencies.
 
• They pitch their calls at a frequency between 20-100 kilohertz, which is very high for humans to hear.
 
• The human ear can hear between__** 20 Hertz to 20,000 Hertz.**__
 
• The waves that they produce are reflected by the object that the waves hit.
 
• Dolphins also function the same way.
 
• This way, the bats get the information of the distance of the object and also of the nature of the reflecting surface.

questions.question: Who founded the Servants of India Society in 1905?
questions.solution:
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
 
• Its objective was to unite and train Indians of different religions and ethnicities in welfare work.

questions.question: In pre-independent India, the British moved the capital of India from Calcutta to Delhi in ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• In pre-independent India, the British moved the capital of India from Calcutta to Delhi in **1911**__.
 
• __**Lord Hardinge**__ proposed this move of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi stating that earlier Calcutta suited trade interests but now a capital must be centrally located for uniform administration.
 
• The decision of capital change was proclaimed (order issued by King George V) in the Delhi Durbar in 1911.
 
• Before that, the Calcutta was the capital of India from 1772.
 
• Since 1947, Delhi has been the capital of India.
 
• Delhi was declared the National capital Region and awarded partial statehood under the __**69th Amendment Act**__.
 
• Shimla was declared as the summer capital of India in 1864.
 
• Indian Councils Act of 1909, legislation passed by the British also known as Morley-Minto reforms, had allowed Indians for the first time to stand for legislative council positions.

 Nehru-Liaquat/Delhi Pact

 Lucknow Pact
 1916
 
 
 
• Friendly relations between the Muslim League and the Indian National Congress (INC).
 
• It was for the first time that the Hindus and the Muslims came together on common ground.
 
• It sowed the seed of belief among the British that India could get a government of Self.
 
• The extremist and moderate faction of the INC also got united.
 
 
 
 

 Poona Pact
 1932
 Agreement between Hindu leaders in India granting new rights to untouchables (low-caste Hindu groups).
 
 

 Gandhi-Irwin Pact
 1931
 
 
 
• A pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy Lord Irwin.
 
• Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-1934) and attend the Round Table Conference.
 
• In return, Irwin will release imprisoned Satyagrahis.
